criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose, rationale, single-spacecraft justification and users are all addressed with literature support. Rationale is persuasive; operator/customer distinction is somewhat loose but adequate for high standard.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major elements covered with STK screenshots and access data. But launch choice is speculative (Vega E not yet built), RAAN justification is weak, no link budget or hand calculations, and EOL text is truncated. Errors and thin evidence keep it at adequate.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved
The proposed ZYZZsat is small and without thrusters in a low-earth orbit.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarises the design and acknowledges launch risk, but is largely a restatement of sections with little quantitative synthesis or specific recommendation.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure and headings are clear, but figures lack numbered captions, references are bare URLs with a Wikipedia source, and there are typos and a broken reference. Writing is readable but not professional.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: RAAN of 27.33° is claimed to indicate launch site location; RAAN is not determined by launch site alone and this is not justified.
No hand calculation shown for the sun-synchronous inclination; only a plot is given.
No link budget or data-rate analysis to support 'sufficient' contact duration.
EOL paragraph is truncated/incomplete; drag sail described but no sizing or deorbit time estimate.
Selects Vega E, which is not yet operational, and relies on a Wikipedia timeline for launch options.
Swath/altitude trade-off asserted qualitatively without resolution or sensor parameters.

overall: A coherent, well-structured mission concept covering all required elements with STK evidence, but weakened by speculative launch choice, missing quantitative calculations, incomplete EOL discussion, poor figure labelling and referencing.

feedback.summary: Your report presents a coherent, well-structured mission concept that covers all required elements with STK evidence and a persuasive rationale. To reach the next level, strengthen the design with quantitative support: justify the launch and RAAN choices, add hand calculations and a link budget, complete the EOL analysis, and tighten figure labelling and referencing.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly states the mission purpose, the need for coral-reef monitoring, the single-spacecraft justification and the users, with literature support. This is Accomplished work. To secure the top of this band, sharpen the operator versus customer distinction and ensure every claim carries a specific reference.
criteria.C2: All major design elements are covered with STK screenshots and access data, but the design sits at Adequate. The Vega E choice is speculative and rests on a Wikipedia timeline; the RAAN justification is weak; there is no link budget or hand calculation for the sun-synchronous inclination; the EOL paragraph is truncated with no drag-sail sizing or deorbit estimate; and the swath/altitude trade-off is left unresolved. To reach Accomplished, resolve these with quantitative evidence and defensible sources.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion restates the design and acknowledges launch risk, which is Adequate. To reach Accomplished, synthesise the evidence quantitatively and give a specific, justified recommendation rather than a section-by-section summary.
criteria.C4: Structure and headings are clear, but figures lack numbered captions, references are bare URLs including a Wikipedia source, and there are typos and a broken reference. To reach Accomplished, add numbered captions, use consistent professional referencing, and proofread for spelling and grammar.

next_steps: Replace the Vega E/Wikipedia launch justification with a currently operational vehicle and a cited, defensible rationale; justify the RAAN choice independently of launch site.
Add hand calculations for the sun-synchronous inclination and a link budget/data-rate analysis supporting the contact duration, and resolve the swath/altitude trade-off with sensor parameters.
Complete the EOL section with drag-sail sizing and a deorbit time estimate, and fix figure captions and referencing (numbered captions, no bare URLs or Wikipedia).
